title: Hado Fishing Experience Village in Jeju: Meet the Island's Haenyeo Sea Divers (Beginner's Guide)
html:
Most first-time visitors to Jeju Island stick to Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak and the main beaches, so they never hear about Hado Fishing Experience Village (하도어촌체험마을). It's a small, working fishing village on Jeju's east coast, in an area called Hado-ri (part of Gujwa-eup township). What makes it special is that you can actually meet and learn from Jeju's famous haenyeo — the island's legendary female sea divers — instead of just reading about them on a plaque somewhere.

What Is Hado Fishing Experience Village?

"Village experience" programs like this one are common all over rural Korea — local fishing or farming communities set up simple facilities so visitors can try real local work instead of just watching from a distance. Hado's version centers on the sea: you can try the kind of diving, snorkeling, and shellfish-gathering that local women have done here for generations. The village is also right next to a quiet stretch of coastline that's part of Jeju's famous Olle-gil coastal walking trail network, so it's an easy add-on if you're already doing a walk along this part of the island.

Meet the Haenyeo: Korea's Legendary Sea Divers

Haenyeo (해녀) means "sea women" in Korean. For centuries, Jeju women have free-dived — no oxygen tanks, just a wetsuit, fins, and trained breath-holding — to gather abalone, conch, and seaweed from the ocean floor, often diving well into their 60s and 70s. It's physically demanding, sometimes dangerous work, and the haenyeo tradition is so culturally important that UNESCO added it to its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2016. The village's Haenyeo Museum walks you through their history, tools, and daily life, which is worth doing before (or instead of) trying the water yourself.

💡 Local tip: Seeing real haenyeo diving in action isn't guaranteed — they work around tides, weather, and their own schedules, not tourist timetables. If you specifically want to watch (or join) a haenyeo-led experience rather than just visit the museum, call ahead and ask what's running that day instead of just showing up.

Hands-On Experiences: Diving, Snorkeling, and Bamboo Pole Fishing

The village runs a few different hands-on programs, and you can usually pick based on how adventurous you're feeling: a guided haenyeo diving experience where you wear real diving gear and try to catch seafood with an instructor nearby, regular snorkeling, and bamboo pole fishing or shore harvesting for a calmer, dry-land-adjacent option. The village website says it's open to visitors ages 3 and up, with room for groups of around 50 people at a time.

The one catch: the official site (하도어촌체험마을.kr) is Korean-only, and online sources don't agree on current prices, so don't rely on a number you find online. Have your hotel, a Korean-speaking friend, or your Jeju tour desk call +82-64-783-1996 ahead of your visit to confirm which programs are running, current pricing, and whether an English-speaking guide is available that day.

Hado Beach and the Migratory Bird Habitat

If you'd rather skip the water activities, the village is still worth a stop for Hado Beach, known for clean, shallow, blue-green water and a quiet stretch of white sand that rarely gets crowded. Right next to it is the Hado-ri Migratory Bird Habitat, a wetland where dozens of bird species — including some rare ones — stop over during migration season. It's a nice, low-key walk if you want to slow down after Jeju's busier attractions.

Practical Info & Getting There

The village is open 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every day of the year, but you should still call ahead before visiting since programs depend on weather and tides. There's free parking on site.

From Jeju City or Jeju International Airport, local buses 201 and 711-2 run out to Hado-ri, followed by about a 20-minute walk to the village — fine if you're not carrying heavy luggage, but a taxi (roughly 40–50 minutes from the airport) or a rental car is much easier, especially with gear. For GPS, search "하도어촌체험마을" or use coordinates 33.5550758560, 126.7982424575 in Google Maps or Naver Map.

💬 Thinking about adding a haenyeo experience to your Jeju trip? Drop your questions in the comments — happy to help you plan it!
meta_description: Meet Jeju haenyeo divers, try snorkeling or bamboo fishing, and relax at Hado Beach at this lesser-known east-coast fishing village.
